name: mkldnn_linear_backward
description: Representative ATen signature (not an exclusive ABI), copied verbatim from the registered schema: aten::mkldnn_linear_backward(Tensor self, Tensor grad_output, Tensor weight, bool[3] output_mask) -> (Tensor, Tensor, Tensor). All supplied registered schemas, verbatim: (1) aten::mkldnn_linear_backward.out(Tensor self, Tensor grad_output, Tensor weight, bool[3] output_mask, *, Tensor(a!) out0, Tensor(b!) out1, Tensor(c!) out2) -> (Tensor(a!), Tensor(b!), Tensor(c!)); (2) aten::mkldnn_linear_backward(Tensor self, Tensor grad_output, Tensor weight, bool[3] output_mask) -> (Tensor, Tensor, Tensor). The representative signature is not exclusive: the original Gems pytest owns the full contract of overloads, keyword arguments, returns, errors, aliasing and mutation, and must never be narrowed to this one signature. Semantics from the tests: aten::mkldnn_linear_backward is the oneDNN (MkldnnCPU) linear/inner-product backward primitive. self and grad_output must be opaque oneDNN (mkldnn layout) tensors of rank >= 2; weight must be a dense fp32 tensor. output_mask is a fixed-size bool[3] (grad_input, grad_weight, grad_bias) with no schema default, so it is always passed explicitly; the default overload is exercised with every one of the eight mask combinations. The default overload returns three Tensors in that order; the frozen tests require each component to match the reference, including None whenever the reference component is None, and accept a rank-0 grad_bias (noted for the case where only the weight is requested) compared only by dim, dtype and layout because its contents are undefined. The .out overload takes keyword-only out0/out1/out2 buffers; that overload is exercised with grad_input requested, and the frozen test asserts that each returned entry is the caller's buffer itself (schema: Tensor(a!)/Tensor(b!)/Tensor(c!) -> (Tensor(a!), Tensor(b!), Tensor(c!)), with the schema annotating those buffers as mutated and the test comparing the requested entries against the reference), while the contents of masked-off buffers are not compared by the test. Error behavior is owned by pytest and is deliberately not modeled here: the supplied pytest asserts a dense (non-mkldnn) self rejection, a non-fp32 weight rejection, a rejection of an output_mask whose length is not 3, a rank-1 self rejection and an int8-operand rejection. The file's header additionally notes that float64/int32/int64/bool/fp8 are rejected by to_mkldnn before the operator, that int8/uint8 convert but have no inner-product backward kernel, and that autograd for this operator itself is not implemented (its three gradient components are covered by the output_mask sweep).
